land.text: the area between Saada and Taiz, taken in 847; Sanaa fell when the governor Himyar ibn al-Harith fled from Yemen
Sanaa, where the dynasty "had lost real power" by 997

successors.note: Infobox lists the Ziyadid dynasty as successor; the page also says Sanaa was lost to a series of rival takeovers, and the clan appears in chronicles until 1280.

capitals.name: Sanaa
capitals.note: Infobox capitals "Shibam Kawkaban and Sanaa" with no years; Muhammad "moved the capital to Shibam" in 872, so Sanaa before is the researcher's reading.

capitals.name: Shibam Kawkaban
capitals.note: Also the refuge in 905-916 when the Ismaili da'is held Sanaa.

rulers.name: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad
rulers.note: murdered his father and uncle in Shibam's mosque; 892-898 or 882-886

rulers.name: Abdallah ibn Qahtan
rulers.note: stopped naming the Abbasids in the khutba and recognised the Fatimid caliph

correction.text: the area between Saada and Taiz

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Yufirid row): "In 847 they took the area between Saada and Taiz." The page gives no area; the highland provinces of modern Yemen from Sa'dah to Ta'izz are the researcher's reading and include some Tihama lowlands the Ziyadids held from 866.

correction.text: the highlands with Janad and Hadramawt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "Muhammad ruled Sanaa, Janad, and Hadramawt from 872, and moved the capital to Shibam." Janad lies near Taiz and is inside the highland shape.

New keyframe: "Qarmatians took Sanaa in 905 and confined the Yu'firids to Shibam Kawkaban. Yu'firid forces retook Sanaa in 916." (The page's Qarmatians are the Ismaili da'is Ibn Hawshab and Ali ibn al-Fadl.)
New keyframe: Sanaa retaken in 916; Sanaa "was lost to a series of rival takeovers" (al-Mukhtar al-Qasim took it in 956 and was murdered that year); by 997 the dynasty "had lost real power in Sanaa".

region.text: the area between Saada and Taiz

ledger.note: 847: Yu'fir of the Dhu Hiwal tribe of Shibam Kawkaban takes the highlands. 'In 847 they took the area between Saada and Taiz. Sanaa fell to their arms when the governor Himyar ibn al-Harith fled from Yemen' (infobox established 847).
872: Muhammad extends the emirate. 'Muhammad ruled Sanaa, Janad, and Hadramawt from 872.'
872: Muhammad ibn Yu'fir 'moved the capital to Shibam' (Shibam Kawkaban).

region.text: Sanaa and the highlands, leaving the Yu'firids Shibam Kawkaban

ledger.counterpart: Ismaili da'is of Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Jayshani
ledger.note: 905: the Ismaili da'is take Sanaa. 'Qarmatians took Sanaa in 905 and confined the Yu'firids to Shibam Kawkaban' (the Ismaili da'is Ibn Hawshab and Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Jayshani).

ledger.counterpart: Ismaili da'is of Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Jayshani
ledger.note: 916: the Yu'firids retake Sanaa. 'Yu'firid forces retook Sanaa in 916.'
997: the dynasty ends. The page gives 997 as the end; Abdallah's son As'ad II succeeded him but 'the dynasty had lost real power in Sanaa'; the infobox names the Ziyadids as successor.

wars.name: Ismaili da'is' conquest of Sanaa
belligerents: Ismaili da'is of Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Jayshani
wars.outcome: The da'is took Sanaa in 905 and confined the Yu'firids to Shibam Kawkaban; the Yu'firids retook it in 916.

wars.name: Abdallah ibn Qahtan's raid on Zabid
wars.outcome: "Successfully attacked the Ziyadids in 989, investing and plundering Zabid." No border moved.

certainty.note: Highland emirate known by its cities (Sanaa, Shibam Kawkaban, Janad); no frontiers on the page. The Tihama lowlands were Ziyadid from 866.

notes: Cliopatria has no Yufirid row (Cliopatria's Ziyadid dynasty row, 866-1138, is the Tihama; the Yufirid highlands appear nowhere). Wikidata id not known; left null. One page opened (the article is thin on territory; the other candidates, Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Jayshani and the Rassid imams, were not opened for budget). The article's own slug on Wikipedia is Yu'firids (Yufirid dynasty gives a not-found page). Disagreements: Muhammad 872-892 or 872-882; Ibrahim 892-898 or 882-886; al-Hadi Yahya briefly held Sanaa in 901 (Zaydi imam), al-Mukhtar al-Qasim in 956: brief takeovers not written as events; Abdallah's 989 raid on Zabid; the Yufirids 'formally deferred to the Ziyadids in the Tihama' (Ziyadid suzerainty, no year; the Ziyadid dossier should carry the vassal tint) and recognised the Fatimid caliph under Abdallah ibn Qahtan (undated). Counterparts needing dossiers: the Zaydi imamate of Yemen (Rassids, 897-; slug rassids or imamate-of-yemen), the Ismaili da'is of Sanaa (905-916) are a rebel/local state. The shape of the highlands is the researcher's reading (Sa'dah to Ta'izz admin units), larger than the realm's likely core.
